topIssues.title: Orchestrator rewrites GitLab subgroup repository URLs to the parent group
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
## Defect

`normalizeRepositoryInput` in `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/repo-input.ts` keeps only two path segments, so `https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/project` becomes `https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup.git`, which can never be a repository (GitLab namespaces cannot hold a project and a subgroup with the same path). The TASKS action's text extractor also captures only two segments. Every coding task for a GitLab subgroup project therefore fails to clone.

Reproduced on develop `811c3fac48`: `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/charts/gitlab` normalizes to `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/charts.git`, and `git ls-remote` on that URL fails, while `…/charts/gitlab.git` lists branches.

## Acceptance

- GitLab URLs keep the full namespace path up to the `/-/` page separator (and legacy page routes).
- GitHub and Bitbucket keep `owner/repo`; existing forms normalize as before.
- Output still passes `assertSafeGitRemote`.

Fix: #33108

topIssues.title: fix(cloud): reject malformed Google disconnect bodies before bulk removal
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`POST /api/v1/eliza/google/disconnect` silently converts malformed JSON to an
empty object. The route then applies its defaults (`side: "owner"`,
`connectionId: null`) and calls `disconnectManagedGoogleConnection`, where a
null connection id means **disconnect every managed Google connection on that
side**.

A truncated or otherwise unreadable request body can therefore become a
successful bulk disconnect instead of a rejected request.

**To reproduce**

Against current `develop` (`27dec7b0c38eb6f38b397758b08be67680bf8d64`):

1. Authenticate as a user with one or more managed owner-side Google
   connections.
2. Send `POST /api/v1/eliza/google/disconnect` with
   `Content-Type: application/json` and the truncated body `{`.
3. Observe HTTP 200 `{ "ok": true }` and a bulk disconnect call.

A deterministic real-Hono-route harness used the production parser, zod
schema, routing, defaults, response, and mutation ordering, with auth and the
Google connector replaced by call-ledger boundaries:

```text
request body: {
HTTP status: 200
disconnectManagedGoogleConnection calls: 1
arguments:
  organizationId: org-1
  userId: user-1
  side: owner
  connectionId: null

focused reproduction: 1 passed, 0 failed, 2 assertions
```

The temporary reproduction file was removed afterward and the contribution
worktree is clean.

**Expected behavior**

- Malformed or unreadable non-empty JSON returns HTTP 400 before the connector
  service is called.
- Syntactically valid but schema-invalid JSON continues to return HTTP 400.
- If the existing API contract intentionally supports a bodyless request or a
  valid `{}` as “disconnect all owner-side connections,” that behavior remains
  explicit and unchanged; it must not be conflated with parse failure.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- Screenshots / recording: N/A — server-only API behavior with no rendered UI.
- Backend logs: N/A — the exact route response and connector call ledger above
  capture the mutation boundary directly.
- Frontend console/network logs: N/A — no frontend behavior changes.
- Real-LLM trajectory: N/A — no model, prompt, provider, or planner behavior.
- Domain artifact: the connector call ledger proves that malformed input reaches
  the bulk-disconnect operation with `connectionId: null`; a live Google account
  was deliberately not mutated for reproduction.

**Duplicate and overlap search**

Repository code, open pull-request file lists, and open/closed issues were
searched for `google disconnect malformed JSON`, `bulk Google disconnect invalid
body`, and `disconnectManagedGoogleConnection malformed`. No existing issue or
open PR covers this route.

topIssues.title: fix(cloud): reject malformed JSON before optional-body mutations
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Several authenticated mutation routes intentionally allow an absent or empty
JSON body, but implement that contract with `request.json().catch(() => ({}))`.
That collapses three different inputs into the same value:

1. a deliberately omitted body;
2. a valid `{}` body;
3. malformed or unreadable non-empty JSON.

Because each affected schema accepts `{}`, a truncated request still performs
the mutation and returns success. The initial audit found this on agent
suspension; a follow-up sweep confirmed the same boundary defect on deployment,
campaign sharing/duplication, cancellation, and internal gateway shutdown.

Confirmed affected routes on current `develop`
(`27dec7b0c38eb6f38b397758b08be67680bf8d64`):

- `POST /api/v1/agents/:agentId/suspend`
- `POST /api/compat/agents/:id/suspend`
- `POST /api/v1/apps/:id/deploy`
- `POST /api/v1/advertising/campaigns/:id/duplicate`
- `POST /api/v1/advertising/campaigns/:id/report/share`
- `POST /api/v1/approval-requests/:id/cancel`
- `POST /api/v1/ballots/:id/cancel`
- `POST /api/v1/oauth-intents/:id/cancel`
- `POST /api/v1/payment-requests/:id/cancel`
- `POST /api/internal/discord/gateway/shutdown`

The Google connector's especially destructive default (`connectionId: null`
means disconnect all connections on a side) is tracked separately in #33073.
The already-open Docker-node drain fix is #33050 / #33051.

**Executed reproduction**

Temporary deterministic Hono-route harnesses exercised the production request
parsing, routing, schemas/defaults, response construction, and ordering relative
to each mutation. Auth, persistence lookup, and mutation services were replaced
with deterministic call ledgers.

```text
/api/v1/agents/:agentId/suspend
malformed JSON:      HTTP 202, enqueueAgentSuspendOnce calls: 1
schema-invalid JSON: HTTP 202, enqueueAgentSuspendOnce calls: 1

/api/compat/agents/:id/suspend
malformed JSON:      HTTP 202, enqueueAgentSuspendOnce calls: 1
schema-invalid JSON: HTTP 202, enqueueAgentSuspendOnce calls: 1

/api/v1/apps/:id/deploy
malformed JSON:      HTTP 202, createDeployment calls: 1

/api/v1/advertising/campaigns/:id/duplicate
malformed JSON:      HTTP 201, duplicateCampaign calls: 1

/api/v1/payment-requests/:id/cancel
malformed JSON:      HTTP 200, payment cancel calls: 1

focused reproduction total: 7 passed, 0 failed, 14 assertions
```

The four remaining listed routes have the same statically verified control
flow: parse failure becomes `{}`, the local schema accepts `{}`, then the route
invokes its mutation service. They were not counted as executed evidence.

All temporary reproduction files were removed afterward and the contribution
worktree is clean.

**Expected behavior / acceptance**

For every retained affected route:

- A genuinely absent, empty, or whitespace-only body keeps the route's existing
  documented optional-body behavior.
- A valid `{}` body keeps the same behavior.
- Malformed or unreadable non-empty JSON returns a structured HTTP 400 before
  the mutation service is invoked.
- Syntactically valid but schema-invalid JSON returns HTTP 400; in particular,
  the two suspend routes must stop replacing invalid `reason` values with the
  default reason.
- Regression tests assert both the response and an empty mutation call ledger
  for malformed input, plus the intended bodyless behavior for each route.
- Any shared parser/helper must preserve route-specific envelopes and must not
  turn this into an unproved API-wide mechanical sweep.

This can be delivered in acceptance-ready slices if maintainers prefer, but the
issue records the confirmed family so fixes are consolidated rather than
rediscovered route by route.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- Screenshots / recording: N/A — server-only API behavior with no rendered UI.
- Backend logs: N/A — exact route responses and mutation call ledgers are
  recorded above.
- Frontend console/network logs: N/A — no frontend behavior changes.
- Real-LLM trajectory: N/A — no agent planner or model behavior is under test.
- Domain artifacts: no live resources were mutated; the route-level service
  call ledgers prove that invalid requests cross each mutation boundary.

**Duplicate and overlap search**

Repository code, open pull-request file lists, and open/closed issues were
searched for malformed/invalid JSON with each mutation name. No existing issue
or open PR covers these routes. #33051 is deliberately limited to the
Docker-node drain route and already has exact-head approvals, so it should not
be expanded after review.

topIssues.title: crypto refunds: a malformed or reused refund key is reported as CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT
topIssues.author: nothingxnowhere
topIssues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`cryptoPaymentRefundsService.refundAsCloudCredits` reports two refund-key problems with the code reserved for an unusable amount.

- `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/crypto-payment-refunds.ts:123-125`: a refund key that fails the `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{7,127}$` pattern throws `CryptoRefundError("CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT", "Refund key is invalid")`.
- `:193-197`: a refund key that was already used for a different amount throws `CryptoRefundError("CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT", "Refund key was already used for a different amount")`.
- `:126-131` is the actual amount check, which throws the same code with "Refund amount must be a positive USD amount with at most six decimals".

The code union (`:37-44`) has no member for a key problem. The messages are right; the typed reason is wrong, which is the same shape as #32945 (a whole-cents amount reported as `AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE`). The repository error policy asks for an actionable `code`; an operator who branches on `CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT` and corrects the amount is chasing the wrong field for both key cases.

Consumers: `git grep CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT` across `packages/` and `plugins/` finds only the service and its test. The operator script (`packages/cloud/scripts/admin/refund-crypto-payment.ts`) prints the thrown error, so it shows the code verbatim.

**To Reproduce**

On `origin/develop` `27dec7b0c3`, Bun 1.3.14, against a PGlite database migrated with `bun run db:cloud:migrate` and holding no rows. A probe calls the real service with three keys (the third is well-formed, so it reaches the payment lookup):

```
$ DATABASE_URL=pglite://<dir> bun --conditions=eliza-source <probe>.ts
{"refundKey":"k","code":"CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT","message":"Refund key is invalid"}
{"refundKey":"bad key with spaces","code":"CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT","message":"Refund key is invalid"}
{"refundKey":"support-ticket-0001","code":"CRYPTO_REFUND_PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND","message":"Crypto payment not found"}
```

The reuse case needs a settled payment; the service test's PGlite fixture reproduces it (refund once with key `support-ticket-3` for 2 USD, then again with the same key for 3 USD) and gets `CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT` from `:193-197`.

**Expected behavior**

- A malformed refund key gets its own code, for example `CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_KEY`, with the current message.
- A refund key reused with a different amount gets its own code, for example `CRYPTO_REFUND_KEY_AMOUNT_MISMATCH`, with the current message and the `paymentId` context.
- `CRYPTO_REFUND_INVALID_AMOUNT` stays for the amount check only. No message, ordering or ledger behaviour changes.

**Screenshots / recording of the wrong behavior (required for anything visible)**

N/A - a service error code with no rendered surface; the probe transcript above is the proof.

**Evidence / reproduction proof**

- [x] MP4 recording or JPG screenshots of the broken behavior: N/A - no visible surface; see the transcript.
- [x] Backend logs and frontend console/network logs when relevant: the service's thrown code and message are in the transcript. N/A for frontend.
- [x] Real-LLM trajectory when the bug involves agent/action/prompt/model behavior: N/A - no model, prompt or action is involved.
- [x] Domain artifacts when relevant: the code and message pairs above, from the real service on a migrated PGlite database.

**Additional context**

- The operator script that surfaces these codes cannot currently start on `develop` (#33054); the probe called the service directly through the `@elizaos/cloud-shared` export.

topIssues.title: LOGS delete and RUNTIME reload_config report success on unacknowledged responses
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
## Defect

Two agent actions report success on a 2xx response that does not carry the route's acknowledgement (the defect 6beb04b5c1 fixed for PLUGIN configure):

- LOGS `delete` (`packages/agent/src/actions/logs.ts`): `resp.json().catch(() => ({}))` and a defaulted `cleared` make a proxy page, `{}`, or `{"cleared":"lots"}` report "Cleared 0 log entries." with `success: true`.
- RUNTIME `reload_config` (`packages/agent/src/actions/runtime.ts`): `{}` or `{"reloaded":false}` reports "No hot-reloadable fields changed." with `success: true`.

Reproduced on develop `27dec7b0c3` with the real handlers and a stubbed fetch.

## Acceptance

- Each op fails with its `*_FAILED` code unless the body matches its route: `{ cleared: <non-negative integer> }` and `{ reloaded: true, applied: string[], requiresRestart: string[] }`.
- Genuine acknowledgements behave as before.

Fix: #33060

topPRs.title: Add durable approved workflows and device actions with managed Cloud identity
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Agent clients need durable, owner-bound workflows and reviewed device operations that survive interruptions, reconnects and process restarts. This change adds generic runtime contracts and persistence for those flows, including managed Cloud Google delegation, hosted results and selected Maps reads.

- Durable workflow authoring, validation, approval receipts, lifecycle changes and hosted delivery retain explicit approval and owner boundaries. Generic approval presentation is authoritative; legacy metadata remains a compatibility reader with downgrade rejection.
- Device actions bind proposals, approval, claim and immutable receipts to authenticated owner, agent and device enrollment. Selected Maps reads require negotiated capability and matching target identity; replay retrieves the bounded historical result without a new device read.
- Managed Cloud owner configuration and Google delegation provide identity and Gmail/Calendar access boundaries with server-side credentials and scope checks.
- Action discovery retains umbrella actions when a resource-specific alias matches, preserving role and context eligibility.
- Workflow mutation replies carry canonical receipts from the actual committed definition. Cancellation provenance is captured under the row lock, with per-service workflow control serialization. Submission, cancellation requests and pending device approvals cannot serve as proof that the requested operation completed. Pending workflow widgets retain their callback delivery.

Validation at prior head 252152eaa0352fd26f4824371e967bbf4e828bfd:

- Focused workflow SQL/worker/settlement/evaluator/parser checks: 7 tests and 243 assertions passed; workflow typecheck and lint passed.
- Device HTTP/PGlite lifecycle and evaluator checks passed, including refusal of false completion claims for pending approval, unknown outcomes and selected reads; assistant and agent typechecks passed.
- Independent source review found no remaining blocker in the receipt correction. Cancellation serialization is per service instance; it is not a cross-process SQLite guarantee.
- Full frozen installation, all284 standard root tasks and audits, emitted host build, twelve compiler cases, packaged Reminder flow and import guard passed with unchanged source. The original aggregate run failed on an unexplained cancellation HTTP reset. Separate unchanged-source workflow recovery passed31/31 files and167 tests; that original failure remains recorded.
- The separately enabled historical compiler-upgrade E2E passed24 assertions with historical source and current dependencies.
- Actual Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b chat completed with seven model calls, created one inactive unscheduled workflow, then a manually reviewed source was explicitly approved and executed once to return56. Removal preserved canonical approval/execution/lifecycle receipts, confirmed by fresh readback. This is local synthetic workflow acceptance.

Hosted CI36908850398 completed successfully at exact head252152eaa0352fd26f4824371e967bbf4e828bfd, including source/build checks, billing replay and PostgreSQL.

Native paired Maps flows, Cloud login/Gmail revocation and physical-device acceptance remain pending. This draft does not establish complete MVP or deployment acceptance.

Current head ab8f9a7110ae adds one bounded correction for model-authored invalid source quotes before any response field or action effects. The exact source validator remains unchanged; a repeated invalid reply fails closed. Actual HTTP/auth/PGlite/planner tests pass four cases, including one pending Maps proposal with rejected draft facts absent from storage. Sixteen owning pipeline cases, production and test-inclusive typechecks and formatting checks pass. Full exact-head qualification and live provider/native acceptance are pending.

topPRs.title: feat: compose resident sessions, recoverable workers and approved device actions
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Mobile resident hosts need authenticated sessions, durable workflow workers that survive a parent restart without repeating uncertain effects, and reviewed device actions. This change composes direct route dispatch, owner sessions, shared compiler/dependency artifact production, canonical workflow reconciliation, approved Workflows navigation and Android Clock handoffs.

Workers reserve a durable generation before importing approved source. POSIX uses private sockets; Windows uses protected named pipes, SID-bound native handles and immutable source publication. Windows workers load trusted built-in PowerShell modules and detach from the parent while retaining RPC pipes. Android recovery authenticates surviving workers and rechecks detached-agent liveness before admitting a new generation. Unproven ownership and interrupted effects remain unknown.

Clock proposals require the enrolled clock.handoff.v1 capability, explicit device review and canonical claim/receipt handling. Set operations bind hour/minute to the current phone timezone. Strict typed receipts distinguish opened, unavailable, denied, failed and unknown; opened establishes only the Clock handoff, never alarm creation or ringing. Date, recurrence and DST-fold selection are outside this handoff contract.

Validation:

- Current head 28ee31f8fc69cb3610aa92e6ae2601c496419d03: owning HTTP/PGlite approval, claim, receipt and replay lifecycle passes; assistant typecheck and package lint pass. Full bun run verify passes in 758.3 seconds with all 29,825 source files unchanged.
- Clock coverage includes all five capability tokens, malformed/duplicate capability rejection, current-message timezone propagation, strict outcome binding, preapproval rejection and no duplicate claim. The product's complete patched runtime also passes the actual HTTP/PGlite lifecycle with before/after source guards; an earlier timeout is retained separately.
- [Normal-hook Windows/platform acceptance](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/37041735574) passed at prior 1129a6: normal installation, both core jobs, native primitives, two backend survivor cases, all 12 helper-startup cases and all 6 Smithers cases. This is evidence for that exact prior source, not a fresh hosted pass at 28ee31.
- [Android resident qualification](https://github.com/AlphaCompute/alphaphone/actions/runs/37045552334) passed its build/archive stage at product 475be7, then native setup failed on unavailable SDK package tools before emulator startup. No native tests ran. The package-list fix is staged in the [product qualification PR](https://github.com/AlphaCompute/alphaphone/pull/1) work.

Keep this PR draft until fresh Android crash/survivor flows and reviewed Clock execution pass. APK builds, emulator flows, full AOSP boot, live integrations and physical-device/user acceptance remain separate gates.

topPRs.title: Fix native reminder plans, controls and review evidence
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Reminder creation and owner replies could omit timing or destination, lose the originating occurrence, repeat legacy review, or move the displayed completion time after the action. Notification taps could also open cached chat without their source message. This keeps creation, resolution, delivery and viewing on the existing pipelines with explicit source and outcome checks.

Changes:
- Validate native timing/destination plans while retaining safe extraction fallback and archive-only cancellation.
- Bind eligible owner controls to the stored occurrence/source and registered executor. Reject malformed or unavailable controls without discovery loops; preserve unknown evidence for retry.
- Consume legacy reply evidence once, retain authored payloads, and display the actual completion payload time.
- Deliver plain reminder text through existing notifications. Hide historical reminder-only panels without rewriting history or generic choices; retain Calendar-specific acknowledgment semantics.
- Publish conversation/message targets after source persistence. Retain navigation until the actual source is applied or authoritatively rejected; transient failure, profile drift and queue eviction keep retry authority.
- Mark the canonical notification read only after guarded successful source navigation. Existing optimistic unread state, authority-scoped rollback and history remain intact; this does not complete or remove a reminder.

Validation: focused PGlite control/review tests, actual URI/navigation-queue/selection tests, real-store rollback tests and affected typechecks passed. The final combined candidate passed 275 focused tests and renderer/package/signer audits. Physical QA verified two powered-on screen-off reminders once each, an older individual alert opening its exact message and returning to Home, and a final OS tap setting its canonical read timestamp with unread count22→21. Prior messages, definitions, notifications, pairing and preferences were preserved. Initial failed cases remain retained.

Android native push transport is tracked separately in #33106. The accepted device scope is powered-on background/screen-off delivery; full shutdown, audible interruption, automatic dossier activation and universal latency/reliability are not claimed. GitHub checks report the current source result independently of the local and device evidence.

topPRs.title: feat(os): AOSP builder, release-key ceremony and device qualification tooling
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Three generic pieces of OS release tooling lived only in a downstream product (extracted from the senior-care product's explicit patch overlay, eliza-research/senior-care): AOSP builder host provisioning, an offline release-key ceremony, and read-only Android device qualification. None of them is product-specific, so they belong next to the existing `packages/os` lock files, `release-trust.json`, `release-key-policy.ts` and `hardware-targets.json`. The product keeps its own key manifest and requirements file and will consume these after its next repin.

# Change

- **`packages/os/android/builder/`**: dry-run-by-default (`--apply` to act) GCE `c3d-highcpu-90` SPOT builder and Intel nested-virtualization Cuttlefish host scripts, a portable Ubuntu 24.04 cloud-init (signature-verified `repo`, data disk that is never reformatted, shell mirror of `assertBuilderCapacity` from `scripts/aosp/build-grizzly-bundle.ts`: 32 physical cores, 128 GiB RAM, 1500 GB total, 600 GiB free) and `bootstrap/sync-aosp.sh`. The sync script reads `android/aosp.lock.json` by default (relative to itself), checks the remote tag object/commit before fetching, the `.repo/manifests` commit before sync, and every locked project and `requiredSourceFiles` after; it supports `--mirror` and `--reference`. While porting, fixed a field shift for lock projects without `tagObject` (the Pixel 11 Pro profile), and added `EXTRA_LABELS` instead of a hard-coded product label. `make bootstrap` (`bootstrap-aosp.ts`) remains the canonical checkout; the README says how the two relate.
- **`packages/os/android/signing/` + `scripts/aosp/{generate,decrypt}-release-keys.ts`**: generic key manifest (releasekey, platform, shared, media, networkstack, sdk_sandbox, bluetooth, nfc, apex, apex_payload, avb, plus Ed25519 `release_manifest`, `contract_release`, `contract_qualification`). Ed25519 fingerprints use exactly the SPKI base64/SHA-256 encodings that `release-key-policy.ts` pins, plus the PEM `release-trust.json` accepts. `--manifest` lets products add their own app keys; manifests are validated (safe names, RSA-4096/8192). Private keys are scrypt/AES-256 PKCS#8 at rest. Both tools refuse to write inside the eliza checkout or any other Git working tree. Runbook in `android/signing/README.md` (generic, no product names).
- **`scripts/android/device-qualify.ts` + `device-qualify-lib.ts`**: read-only adb (fixed allowlist) / fastboot (`getvar` only) qualification against `--requirements FILE`, defaulting to the new `android/device-requirements/treble-gsi.json` (Treble, vendor API, kernel floor, ABI, dynamic partitions, SELinux, A/B preferred, unlockable/avb_custom_key). Product thresholds (RAM, cameras, radios) stay in product files. Records go to `test-results/os-device-qualification/`; emulator captures are labelled `emulator-observation`. Requirements files are validated (unknown checks rejected). Documented as complementary to the `hardware-targets.json` admission gate.

Risk: additive only; no existing script, lock or trust file changes behaviour. No cloud resource, key or device is touched by tests.

# Testing

- `node --test scripts/__tests__/aosp-builder-infra.node.test.ts scripts/__tests__/release-key-ceremony.node.test.ts scripts/__tests__/device-qualify.node.test.ts` (from `packages/os`, Node 24.15.0, macOS arm64, shellcheck 0.11 and PyYAML present): **34/34 pass**. Covers `bash -n` + shellcheck of all scripts including cloud-init-embedded ones, dry runs with fake `gcloud`/`repo` first on `PATH` proving nothing is invoked, sync dry runs for every profile in `aosp.lock.json` (workspace and mirror), avbtool known-answer vectors (2048: `8a1378f7…a3cb`, 4096: `3672bd6c…f0de`, verified against AOSP `avbtool.py extract_public_key`), a full test-key ceremony + decrypt round trip, `loadReleaseKeyPolicy` acceptance of generated Ed25519 fingerprints, output-location refusals, and a CLI run with a fake adb that asserts only allowlisted commands are sent.
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/shellcheck -x --severity=style` on all builder scripts: clean.
- Biome 2.5.14 `check` on all changed TS/JSON files: clean.
- `node scripts/verify-os-repository-layout.ts`: pass.
- `node --test scripts/__tests__/*.node.test.ts` (whole `test:release` node lane): 488 tests, 472 pass, 13 fail, 3 skipped. The same 13 fail on pristine `develop` 27dec7b0c3 on this host (install-lock, release-safety, AVD timeout, legacy ISO, packaged writer, RISC-V tests; macOS host tooling). `bun test scripts/__tests__/*.bun.test.ts`: 8 pass / 17 fail, identical on pristine develop.
- Root audits run individually: `audit-scripts`, `audit-test-lane-membership`, `audit-focused-skipped-tests`, `audit-tee-secret-leak`, `check-generated-system-files`: all pass.

- [x] Targets `develop` and has no conflicts with the latest `origin/develop` (based on 27dec7b0c3).
- [ ] Ran `bun install` and `bun run verify` after syncing; `bun install` ran, full `bun run verify` not run (see Known gaps).
- [x] Updated relevant documentation (`android/README.md`, `android/builder/README.md`, `android/signing/README.md`).

# Evidence Gate

topPRs.title: Enable configured Android reminder push delivery
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Android reminders could skip Firebase resources, lose delivery priority, re-alert on read updates or miss the event bus during startup. A connected Android renderer could also create a second OS alert alongside FCM. This fixes the configured push path and gives confirmed Android push delivery ownership of the OS alert while preserving the durable in-app notification.

Google Services is loaded for present configuration and malformed configuration fails visibly. Reminder/high/urgent priority reaches FCM; read updates do not re-alert. The sender waits for the registered event bus before subscribing. Native registration retries through the existing app-resume event after permission is granted.

Token registration now reports whether the current host has an attached, configured transport. The Android renderer waits for registration to settle and suppresses its local OS projection only when the current authenticated authority confirms push delivery. Unavailable transport retains the local fallback; authority changes fence stale registration and delivery. Incoming notifications still enter the canonical in-app center.

The native foreground-service caption starts with unknown connection status. Settings hides the optional per-app permission inventory only for its unsupported404 response; genuine permission/error handling remains available.

Validation: combined source606c passed full repository verification,17 owning UI notification tests,11 real boot cases and the persisted backend transport acceptance. All seven files in this update exactly match that verified source. Earlier Gradle/configuration checks and physical app-absent FCM delivery are retained. The final606c QA APK passed build/artifact audit and upgraded with the same signer; all10 shared preference files remained byte-exact. In one bounded physical background run, a naturally due reminder produced exactly one canonical notification and one FCM-tagged Android OS alert, with no local OS alert. This observation does not independently prove WebSocket consumption by the UI; red/green renderer tests cover FCM-owned arrival handling. Fully powered-off durable recovery and final personal QA remain separate. This PR stays draft; no universal push reliability or production rollout acceptance is claimed.


### Negotiated Android reminder data delivery
Android devices advertise the native reminder-data receiver only when the app-owned Firebase handler is present. Reminder pushes then use non-collapsible data messages with a canonical notification ID; older clients retain notification-plus-data behavior. The receiver respects permission/channel settings and retains safe source selectors for cold taps. SafePush registration now happens before Capacitor exports the initial renderer method list, so negotiation works on the actual app.

Validation: native16, backend2, UI20, lifecycle23 and Android policy67 tests passed, plus four owning typechecks. The signed QA app physically negotiated the capability, produced one canonical Android alert and one inbox record, and returned to the expected plain reminder on a warm tap. Existing preferences and history were preserved. Two-reminder powered-off queue recovery and the cold tap to the older source remain pending; these are not claimed as passed. Separate conversation/message source binding is in draft33096.
